subject: Admin activity provenance + DLP-friendly snapshot for compliance review
messages:
From: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@greenbridgehealth.org>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-team@clearwell.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: admin activity snapshot + provenance for SIG review

Hi Kimberly —

GreenBridge is preparing the SIG/SOC2 evidence package for our external audit next month. Can you confirm the following for Redwood-admin activity exports so we can complete our control mapping?

1) Scope: which admin actions are captured (console role changes, service account creation, token issuances, model deployments, policy changes, manual data exports)?
2) Retention: what are default retention windows for hosted vs dedicated vs private? Ability to extend for legal holds?
3) Export formats: what output formats do you support for a full-time-range export and for an incremental delta? CSV/NDJSON/CloudTrail-style?
4) Provenance: can you provide per-file checksums and a signed manifest (HMAC or GPG) to establish chain-of-custody?
5) DLP/redaction: we need an export suitable for review that strips or tokenizes PII (emails, IPs, user identifiers). What redaction modes do you support?
6) Lead time & delivery: typical SLA for ad-hoc slices (e.g., 90-day window) and options for secure delivery (pre-signed S3, SFTP, physical handoff?).

If you have a short sample manifest and an example export schema we can attach to the SIG workbook, that would be ideal. Thanks — we can sync if it's easier over a quick call.

—Sandra
Sandra Lopez
Director, Information Security
GreenBridge Health

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@greenbridgehealth.org>
Cc: audit-team@clearwell.com, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity snapshot + provenance for SIG review

Sandra —

Thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary; I attached a short example manifest and a CSV sample extract (admin_activity_manifest_v1.csv) to this thread.

Quick answers up-front:
- Scope: Redwood logs privileged admin console actions (role/grant/revoke), operator sessions, service-account key events, token issues/rotations, model deployment events (version, rollouts, canaries), configuration changes to routing/batching, and manual exports initiated through the console or API. We also capture session metadata (actor, origin IP, user agent), request IDs, and correlated runtime shard ids.
- Retention: Hosted API: default 365 days for admin activity. Dedicated: 365 days by default; customers can extend to multi-year retention as part of Dedicated contracts. Private: configurable by the customer (we provide tooling and packages to export or mirror logs for long-term archival). Legal hold: we can freeze slices for the requested window and provide an attestable export.
- Export formats: NDJSON and compressed CSV are supported for full exports. We also provide a CloudTrail-style JSON export (field-aligned to help SIEM ingestion). Incremental/delta exports are supported using sequence tokens — i.e., you can request events after a given cursor.
- Provenance: We produce a signed manifest containing per-file SHA256 checksums and a manifest HMAC signed with Redwood's export key. For Dedicated/Private we can use a signed KMS envelope or customer-supplied key to sign the manifest. The attached export-checksum.sha256 is an example.
- DLP/redaction modes: 
  * NONE: raw export (for forensics).
  * PSEUDONYMIZE: replace user emails and IDs with deterministic tokens (token map retained separately under controlled access).
  * REDACT: remove/blank PII fields (email, IP) entirely from the export.
  * TRUNCATE: keep suffix/anonymized hash for correlation but not full identifier.

- Delivery & SLA: For a standard on-demand slice (up to 90 days) our typical turnaround is 3 business days for Hosted. Expedited 24–48 hour delivery can be requested for an additional fee or via an enterprise SLA. Delivery modes: pre-signed S3 URLs (preferred), SFTP with client certs, or encrypted bundle on secure courier for very large/air-gapped needs.

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) can add technical details about timestamp fidelity, canonicalization, and manifest format. If the auditor needs sample files directly in the SIG workbook, we can provide the NDJSON sample and a redacted pseudonymized sample.

Best,
—Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: admin_activity_manifest_v1.csv, export-checksum.sha256

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@greenbridgehealth.org>
Cc: audit-team@clearwell.com
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity snapshot + provenance for SIG review

Sandra/Kimberly —

Adding the technical specifics you asked for so the auditors have the exact expectations:

- Schema & fields (sample): event_id, occurred_at (ISO-8601 UTC w/ microseconds), actor_type, actor_id (pseudonymizable), action, target_type, target_id, resource_version, request_id, origin_ip (redaction options), user_agent, region, shard_id, ingestion_offset.
- Timestamp: canonicalized to UTC in export; we include original timezone in a metadata header when available. Format example: 2026-11-24T23:12:03.123456Z.
- Checksum & manifest: each file is compressed with gzip; we compute SHA256 over the compressed file. The manifest is a line-delimited JSON list with filename, size_bytes, sha256_hex, record_count, sequence_range, and a manifest_version. The final manifest is HMAC-SHA256-signed. For Dedicated customers we can instead provide an RSA-signed manifest using a customer-managed key.
- Canonicalization: we normalize record ordering (time asc) and strip volatile ephemeral fields (local cache pointers) to ensure deterministic checksums.
- Deltas & cursors: exports can be generated by start/end sequence token or by time range. For high-volume tenants we support an incremental stream export where the consumer can request records since sequence N.
- Audit-proofing: we include an export metadata envelope (export_time, requested_by, request_id, redaction_mode, retention_window_at_request) and a signed attestation statement that Redwood produced the bundle at the stated time.
- Encryption in transit: all deliveries are TLS1.2+/SFTP with mutual auth; at-rest bundles are AES-256-GCM encrypted and can be wrapped with the customer's KMS key when requested.

I can share the exact manifest schema if the auditors want the JSON schema file.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sandra Lopez <sandra.lopez@greenbridgehealth.org>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: audit-team@clearwell.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: admin activity snapshot + provenance for SIG review

Sandra —

Thanks for the detailed ask and thanks Ben / Kimberly for the quick turnaround. Proposed operational plan to formalize this:

1) We will prepare two bundles for your SIG workbook: (A) a pseudonymized NDJSON bundle (PSEUDONYMIZE) and (B) a raw NDJSON bundle for on-site review under a confidentiality addendum. Both bundles will include the signed manifest and export checksum files.
2) SLA: standard delivery within 3 business days of signed request; expedited 48-hour delivery available if GreenBridge confirms priority.
3) Delivery method: please confirm preference. We recommend pre-signed S3 for integrity and speed. If you require SFTP, provide the host + public key.
4) Proof-of-export: bundle will include export-checksum.sha256 and a manifest signed with HMAC; we will also provide an attestation email with the export_time and request_id.

Action items for GreenBridge:
- Confirm redaction mode (PSEUDONYMIZE vs REDACT) and delivery method.
- Provide the SFTP public key or S3 destination role if you prefer push delivery.

If you want, we can run a short verification exercise where we produce a 7-day sample slice and you validate the manifest and checksums against the sample.

Regards,
—Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

P.S. I attached a DLP guidance doc (dlp-redaction-guidance.pdf) with examples of the pseudonymization mapping strategy and an example manifest layout.
